newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab says leasing behind U.S. sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Saab says leasing behind U.S. sales rise.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. car maker Saab Automobile AB said on Friday that a 70 percent jump in its U.S. car sales in December stemmed from adopting competitors' more advantageous pay programmes on private leasing.
"During the autumn, we saw that competition was very tough," company spokesman Olof Wallen told Reuters.
"Others had more advantageous programmes and U.S. customers look at what monthly costs amount to. We have adjusted to that."
Wallen declined to give any forecasts for 1997, but said that earlier targets were still valid.
"We have a target of 150,000 cars (annually) at the turn of the century worldwide," he said. "We are still aiming for that."
In 1996, the company's worldwide sales amounted to about 100,000 units, he said.
